text: {"voteValue":"REJECT","rationale":"Fails on the load-bearing requirement. The payload asserts zero_execution_consumers:true while simultaneously specifying that 'downstream execution tiers consume signed cryptographic state roots and authorization receipts' — an authorization receipt that gates execution is an execution-effect consumer. The guarantee is asserted, not constructed: no mechanism distinguishes advisory proof emission from permissioning, and no test or invariant is given by which the property could be checked. Second, the stopEpoch design is unsound as written: 'instantaneously invalidates all active grants' is unachievable over the asynchronous pull-based attestation path it also mandates. Absent a bounded staleness window, mandatory fail-closed TTL on cached roots, and a defined recovery/resume procedure after a stop, the register is advisory in practice — the failure mode this control exists to prevent. Third, it is not an 'exact' architecture at R3: no interfaces, schemas, key registry rotation/revocation, ledger persistence, or mapping to repositoryHead. Also unimplementable specifics: FIPS 140-3 Level 4 HSM attestation, and a unidirectional diode ingress contradicting operational epoch-scoped grant administration."}
